newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CBOT soy price fall fails to lure Chinese buyers.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy price fall fails to lure Chinese buyers.

text.p: The sharp overnight drop of soybean and soymeal futures prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) failed to attract buying interest from China as levels were still seen as too high, traders said on Tuesday.
"I think even with today's so-called collapse, (prices are) still above market expectations," said one grains trader.
Others saw the CBOT drop as a short term dip in an otherwise firming market.
"It's true that the price dropped, but the trend is upwards," said a China-based trader.

The CBOT soybean July contract slid 20-1/2 U.S. cents to close on Monday at US$8.68-1/2 a bushel after the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) said 1996/97 soybean ending stocks were unchanged at 125 million bushels.
The news dissapointed the market and also led to the July CBOT soymeal contract falling $8.50 to finish at $285.80 a ton.
The domestic price of soybeans remained at around 3,000 to 3,100 yuan per tonne, while meal in the domestic Chinese market was seen at about 2,800 yuan per tonne.
